name: Data Analyzer: Excel export stores formula-looking cell text as plain text
objective: Proves that cell contents starting like a formula (a known way to run commands or leak data when a spreadsheet is opened) are saved as text, unchanged, and not as live formulas.
precondition: Offline. A spreadsheet is created in memory from made-up data and read back with a spreadsheet-reading library; no spreadsheet program is opened.

steps.action: Export a table with one column of 8 hostile strings and one of numbers
steps.data: '=HYPERLINK(...)', '+1+1', '-2+3', '@SUM(A1:A2)', and the same with leading spaces, tab, carriage return and newline before '='
steps.expected: Every cell in the Data sheet is stored as text and its value equals the original (a carriage return comes back as a line break). No cell in any sheet is a formula

name: Data Analyzer: Excel export stores formula-looking column headers as plain text
objective: Proves hostile column names are also safe.
precondition: Offline. A spreadsheet is created in memory from made-up data and read back with a spreadsheet-reading library; no spreadsheet program is opened.

steps.expected: All four header cells are stored as text and the first keeps its original text

name: Data Analyzer: Excel 'Issues' sheet stores formula-looking text as plain text
objective: Proves the list of found problems is safe even when the problem value or message is hostile.
precondition: Offline. A spreadsheet is created in memory from made-up data and read back with a spreadsheet-reading library; no spreadsheet program is opened.

steps.action: Export a one-cell table with one issue whose value is "=cmd|' /C calc'!A0" and message is '=Bad value'
steps.expected: An 'Issues' sheet exists, no cell anywhere is a formula, and both hostile strings appear unchanged in that sheet

name: Data Analyzer: Real numbers, dates and yes/no values stay typed in the Excel export
objective: Proves the protection does not turn genuine data, including negative numbers, into text.
precondition: Offline. A spreadsheet is created in memory from made-up data and read back with a spreadsheet-reading library; no spreadsheet program is opened.

steps.action: Export a table with negatives (-5, -0.25, 3), three dates and True/False values
steps.expected: Numbers keep their values and numeric type, the date cell is a real date, and the yes/no cell is true

name: Data Analyzer: Highlight colours and comments still work on protected cells
objective: Proves the safety change does not remove the export's colour coding and notes.
precondition: Offline. A spreadsheet is created in memory from made-up data and read back with a spreadsheet-reading library; no spreadsheet program is opened.

steps.action: Export a two-row table ('=1+1', 'fine') with an error issue on row 0 and a warning on row 1
steps.expected: Cell A2 is text '=1+1' with red-ish fill (FFCCCB); A3 has orange-ish fill (FFE5B4); A2 carries the comment 'bad one'

name: Data Analyzer: Formula-detection helper gives the right yes/no for 10 sample values
objective: Proves the helper that decides whether text looks like a formula is correct for typical and non-text inputs.

steps.action: Ask the helper about each value
steps.data: '=1', '+1', '-1', '@x', ' \t=x' (should be yes); 'hello', 'a=b', empty text, the number 5, nothing (should be no)
steps.expected: Yes for the first five and no for the other five
